controller like Kyverno only lets signed images from our registry run.<br>At runtime Pod Security Standards (restricted) block root and privileged pods, and we keep rescanning what's running."" text.tspan: Securing container images: build → scan → sign → store → admit → run
Continuous: rescan images already running (new CVEs appear daily) · Inspector / Trivy Operator reports
rebuild on base-image updates (Renovate/Dependabot) · NetworkPolicy + least-privilege RBAC/IRSA limit damage
"Security starts in the Dockerfile: small base, multi-stage, non-root, no secrets in layers. CI scans every image with
Trivy and fails the build on fixable critical CVEs; we push to private ECR with immutable tags and deploy by digest.
Images are signed with cosign, and an admission controller like Kyverno only lets signed images from our registry run.
At runtime Pod Security Standards (restricted) block root and privileged pods, and we keep rescanning what's running."
